Package hadur2.core

package hadur2.core
Hadur 2's core: the whole of the robot's strategy, as plain Java that never sees the Robocode engine.

Hexagonal architecture. The core is the inside of a hexagon. It takes one BotInput a tick (the robot's state and the events that arrived with it) and returns one BotOrders; it writes line records to a Telemetry and keeps opponent profiles in a ProfileStore. The adapter in the hadur-robot module (hadur2.Hadur) is the only code that touches the engine: it turns engine events into BotEvent values, builds the input from the getters, applies the orders through the setters, and backs the store with Robocode's data directory. That split is what lets the core be replayed, fuzzed and fault-injected without an engine.

The ArchUnit rules in hadur2.core.arch.ArchitectureTest enforce the boundary on every build. The core depends on nothing from robocode.* and uses only the JDK's java.lang, java.util and java.awt.geom (CORE-1). It holds no unseeded randomness, threads, reflection, file or other I/O, and no clock (RES-6), and no mutable static state, so two cores never share anything and the same inputs always give the same orders (CORE-2). This package itself holds the three classes the adapter talks to.

  • HadurCore: the conductor. One instance lives for the whole battle (Robocode makes a new robot object each round, so the adapter keeps it static), which is how learning survives from round to round. Since A2 it drives two brains, the DuelController and the MeleeController, each through the conductor's seam for it, behind the Role contract.
  • Guard: wraps every core tick and returns safe orders if the core throws or returns nothing (RES-1).
  • RoundStats: the round's counters and the R record that carries every fault and degradation counter to the bench report (RES-5). A2 moved it to the kernel's model, so the Duel keeps its counters without seeing the conductor.

The tick. Robocode runs a robot's event handlers inside execute() and then returns to run(); the core keeps that order. The adapter queues the tick's events, builds the input and calls Guard.tick(hadur2.core.model.BotInput), which calls HadurCore.tick(hadur2.core.model.BotInput):

  1. The RoleResolver picks the tick's role, failing closed to the duel: melee only in a Melee-charter battle while two or more opponents are alive, no sentry is alive or has been scanned this round, melee has not thrown this round and the duel has not yet driven this round (ROLE-2 to ROLE-4, GATE-2 to GATE-4). A melee that has just ended hands over to a clean duel at full speed (MELEE-2).
  2. The events. In a Melee charter every non-sentry scan, hit and death goes first to the World (WORLD-1; GATE-5 keeps sentries out of everything); each event is offered to the roles of the charter, Melee before Duel (ROLE-5). While the Duel drives, the duel opponent's scan makes a gun wave and a candidate enemy wave, and the energy ledger turns only unexplained energy drops into firing waves (WAVE-1, WAVE-2). Bullet events feed the ledger, the hit windows, the shield detector and the bullet shadows; the adapter's TickTime and skipped turns feed the tick budget (TIME-1, TIME-2).
  3. The driving role's main body, with the conductor's fire permission (WEAVE-3). Melee: the melee brain's radar, destination and aim. Duel: fire the shot aimed last tick and aim the next, break the waves that have passed us, check the profile's seeds against live evidence (RES-4), step the distance, endgame and flavour policies, update the shadows, surf (or ram), and sweep the radar back to a lost enemy (RADAR-1).
  4. With sentries on the field, the duel's orders are checked against their border (GATE-3). The orders go back through the guard to the adapter.

Units follow Robocode throughout: positions in px (x east, y north), angles in radians with headings absolute (0 = north, clockwise) and bearings relative to the robot's heading, time in ticks, energy and bullet power in the engine's units (power in [0.1, 3.0]). A guess factor is in [-1, 1]: the fraction of the maximum escape angle a target reached, signed by the direction it was moving when the wave was fired.

Subpackages. Each is described in full by its own classes; the requirement IDs are those of docs/requirements.md.

  • model: the port values (BotInput, BotEvent, BotOrders), robot states and their bounded logs, Wave (precise intersection, guess factors, shadowed fractions) and the WaveManager, and the shared seed weight (ADAPT-3). Must not depend on gun, move or replay.
  • physics: Angles and Rules, identical to Robocode's, the battle field and the MovementPredictor that runs the engine's movement rules forward. Must not depend on gun, move, replay or knn.
  • knn: the weighted KD-tree and the KnnViews the gun and the surf keep their samples in, capped in size (RES-2), with k shared out by the tick budget (TIME-1).
  • ledger: the EnergyLedger, which explains the enemy's energy changes between scans by our hits, its refunds, wall hits and collisions, so only a corrected drop in [0.1, 3.0] becomes a wave (WAVE-1, WAVE-2). A leaf on the engine's rules: it may depend only on physics and the JDK.
  • gun: the GunController, the main KNN gun, the anti-surfer gun and the virtual guns that rate them. It takes the opening book's and the policies' decisions through its own setters (ADAPT-1, ADAPT-3). Gun and move never depend on each other.
  • move: wave surfing. The MoveController holds the enemy's waves and the danger views; BulletShadows takes out the firing angles our own bullets would meet (MOVE-1); the SurfMover turns danger into orders, with go-to surfing (MOVE-2) and the ram (END-2).
  • memory: opponent memory for duels (MEM-1 to MEM-5, RES-3): lineage keys, the profile and its checksummed codec, the round folder and the library that loads, saves and evicts; Estimate, a rate with its Agresti-Coull margin (DIAL-1); the tiers. A leaf that reaches storage only through the port; no gun, move, knn, ledger, melee, physics or model code may depend on it.
  • adapt: recognise and adapt (ADAPT-1 to ADAPT-3, RES-4): the OpeningBook that reads a profile once, the seed loader and the seed trust. It sees only memory, the model and the JDK, never BotInput or BotEvent (DIAL-2), and the lower packages never see it.
  • policy: aggressive and unhittable (DIST-1, POW-1, POW-2, END-1, END-2, MOVE-2, TIME-1, TIME-2): rolling hit windows, the distance controller, the power policy, the endgame and the enemy's gun heat, the movement flavour and the TickBudget. It sees only memory, physics and the JDK (DIAL-2), and gun, move and the lower packages never see it.
  • shield: the bullet-shielding counter (SHIELD-1, SHIELD-2): the ShieldDetector and the deterministic AimJitter.
  • role: the role contract's routing (ROLE-1 to ROLE-4, GATE-2 to GATE-5), folded in from the melee extension's posture at A1. The Charter is fixed from the battle's facts before the first tick; the RoleResolver picks the role each tick, latches the round so the role only steps down, and remembers sentry names for the battle; the DuelFocus names the one opponent the duel fights while several are alive (the closest when the duel takes over, kept until it dies); the SentryFence simulates the duel's orders a few ticks ahead and replaces them with a drive to the centre if they would take the robot near the sentries' border. A leaf on the model and physics that only this package sees, so neither brain can tell which role is on.
  • melee: the melee brain, driven each tick by the MeleeController. It reads the World, world's per-round tracker of every opponent that drops the dead at once and infers shots from unexplained energy drops of 0.1 to 3.0 (MSENSE-1, MSENSE-2); a radar that spins with four or more opponents alive and turns toward the one scanned longest ago with two or three (MRADAR-1, MRADAR-2); minimum-risk movement over a ring of candidate points, weighting the points where Hadur would be an opponent's closest robot and the virtual bullets of each inferred shot, and tightening its ring with two opponents left (MMOVE-1 to MMOVE-4); a target selector with a switching margin (MELEE-5); a circular gun with a linear fallback that fires no more than the kill needs (MELEE-6) and holds fire at a target whose last scan is too old (MELEE-7); and a strategy that keeps clear of two opponents fighting each other (MMOVE-5). It depends only on the model, physics and the JDK, and no duel package may depend on it (GATE-1). The plan's later groups, MGUN and MMEM, belong to its M4 and M5 stages.
  • port: the outbound interfaces, Telemetry and ProfileStore, with the in-memory store for tests and the bench. Must not depend on gun, move or replay.
  • replay: the line codec and the Replay driver that run a recorded battle back through a fresh core and guard, checking CORE-2 end to end.

The duel's packages (adapt, gun, knn, ledger, memory, move, physics, policy, shield) are pinned by source hash in DuelIdentityTest as of the melee extension's M0, so melee work cannot change how Hadur fights a duel. Everything that grows during a battle is capped (RES-2).
